description: Everything that touches the chain: watcher liveness for all five chain-event watchers, the capacity-bond and active-staker registries, seller and buyer payment flow, and the slash-risk signals. Thresholds here match monitoring/decdn-node/prometheus-alerts.yml rather than sitting looser than the pages.

panels.title: Watcher tick age
panels.description: Age of each watcher's last successful poll tick, stamped every tick including idle ones, so this is a positive liveness signal rather than an absence of errors. Built with label_replace on the raw selector because `time() - x` drops __name__. Red at 180s matches the stalled-watcher alerts. A watcher that has never ticked reads 0, so the `> 0` guard drops its tick age; if its poll keeps failing, the row shows its down-seconds (time since the first failed tick) instead, matching the stalled-watcher alerts' second arm. A watcher that is simply not wired on this node shows no row.

panels.title: Watcher downtime
panels.description: True time spent in error/backoff. Reads 0 for the whole life of an established cycle, and i64::MAX on a poisoned internal lock — the safe direction. Prefer this over the restart-rate below: the restart counter is edge-triggered through a lock whose update is skipped on poisoning, so it can freeze silently.

panels.title: Watcher restarts
panels.description: Edge-triggered: one increment per healthy-to-error transition, not per backoff iteration.

panels.title: Watcher task panics
panels.description: Any non-zero value is a bug, raised by a Drop guard in resumable_watcher::run.

panels.title: Watcher persistence and chain RPC
panels.description: Boot read retries counts transient-error retries of boot-time chain reads; the metrics listener binds after them, so it reads as a value since start, not a rate. A rise after a restart points at the RPC provider. Fee-shares watcher unregistered is 1 when the startup feeRouter() read failed: the watcher never started, its downtime gauge reads healthy, and the operator share stays at the floor until restart.

panels.title: eth_getLogs window span
panels.description: Block span of the shared chain-event poller's next eth_getLogs window, per node, and the rate of windows the RPC provider rejected for their range or result count. The span starts at blockchain.get_logs_max_block_span, drops to half a rejected window, and doubles back after 32 accepted windows, so a caught-up node climbs back to the ceiling after a transient rejection. Rejections that keep coming mean the provider caps eth_getLogs: set the ceiling to the lowest span reached while they come. Retries/s counts in-tick retries of eth_getLogs windows after a transient provider error (up to two per window); a retry that succeeds is not watcher downtime, so a steady retry rate shows an unreliable provider. The info log line of each retry gives the cause. Deferred/s counts windows that failed every retry: the tick ends there and the next tick resumes at the window, which is not watcher downtime either; the tick fails only after 2 minutes with no tick reaching head.

panels.title: Active staker set
panels.description: Each node's cached view of the active-staker set. Divergence between nodes means one of them is working from stale chain state.

panels.title: Capacity-bond registry resync age
panels.description: Time since the last successful getRegisteredNodes enumeration. The `> 0` guard drops a node that has not bootstrapped yet rather than reporting it as infinitely stale.

panels.title: Registry failures
panels.description: A dropped nodeIdOf lookup means a Reinstated or UnbondingRequested event never landed, so the cached active set has drifted from chain state for that operator until the next full resync.

panels.title: Active nodes by country
panels.description: Active stakers per declared region (ADR 030), from each selected node's CapacityBond registry. Every node holds the whole network, so the query takes the max across nodes, not the sum. A node with a frozen watcher keeps its last view, and max can hold a departed region on the map: check watcher downtime above. A code absent from Grafana's country gazetteer has no location and is not drawn. In current Grafana these are the user-assigned codes (AA, QM–QZ, XA–XZ, ZZ) plus XK and SS. The table to the right lists every region, including these.

panels.title: Active nodes per region
panels.description: Every region the map reads, including codes the map cannot place.

panels.title: Active nodes without a region
panels.description: Active stakers whose on-chain regionHint is empty or not an accepted region code. These nodes are absent from the map and the table. Non-zero means an operator should run `decdn node update-region`; the panel follows on the next watcher tick.

panels.title: Blacklist enforcement failures
panels.description: Distinct hashes a batched re-scope could not re-verify or evict this pass. While non-zero the deny-set is not fully enforced and a blacklisted blob may still be servable.

panels.title: Lanes open
panels.description: Distinct (pool, signer, provider) keys carrying unredeemed vouchers.

panels.title: Unredeemed value
panels.description: Raw 6-decimal USDC base units scaled to dollars. Sums owed minus paid across accepted vouchers, refreshed once per redeemer self-tick.

panels.title: Redemption failures
panels.description: Redemption steps that failed: a redeemMany that reverted or was refused at send, or a lane the redeemer could not plan or load. An unconfirmed receipt does not count here; the On-chain transaction outcomes panel shows it as receipt failed or timeout. From decdn v0.3.0, neither does a send that failed with no tx hash; that panel shows it as maybe broadcast. Skipped — pool unresolved counts lanes kept out of a submit because their pool stayed unknown after the pre-submit getPool: the read faulted, which clears on a later cycle, or the chain shows the pool absent or Closed, which logs a warn! naming it and keeps its lanes out.

panels.title: Lane and receipt-log writes
panels.description: Lane flush failures are background lane-store flushes that failed. Each retries on the next tick, but the frontier a crash would replay keeps growing (DecdnLaneFlushFailures). Dropped or failed receipt writes are lost audit-log rows, not lost revenue.

panels.title: Settlement watcher freshness
panels.description: Age of the settlement watcher's last successful poll tick. A watcher that has never ticked reads 0, so the `> 0` guard drops its tick age; if its poll keeps failing, the series shows its down-seconds (time since the first failed tick) instead, matching DecdnSettlementWatcherStalled's second arm.

panels.title: On-chain transaction outcomes
panels.description: Every settlement redeemMany counts once by outcome (openPool, topUp and reclaim do not count here). A receipt wait that fails or times out falls back to fetching the receipt by hash, and a receipt found there counts as landed or reverted. receipt failed and timeout are the transactions still unconfirmed after that fetch; they can still mine, and their tx hash is in the warn! line. maybe broadcast is a send that failed with no tx hash (a timeout, a reset, an HTTP 5xx, or an `already known`, `nonce too low` or `replacement transaction underpriced` answer): it can be in a mempool or have mined, and the claims stay for the next sweep; or it collided at one nonce with this node's buyer service, which shares the key, and broadcast nothing. It is counted from decdn v0.3.0, and DecdnRedemptionMaybeBroadcast alerts on it. receipt recovered is not an outcome: it counts the waits the fetch by hash resolved, which points at a lagging RPC provider.

panels.title: Vouchers, redemptions and grace closes
panels.description: vouchers accepted counts signed vouchers on inbound streams. reveals accepted counts PayWord preimage reveals that advanced a lane's chain frontier; reveals are not vouchers. vouchers redeemed counts lane claims that landed on chain — one cumulative voucher per lane. A grace close is a pool its owner is closing while this node still holds unredeemed vouchers on it. Watermark reconciles landed counts pre-redeem getWatermarks batches that decoded: the attempt signal behind the already-reconciled skips on the Redemption failures panel. A redeemer submitting claims with this flat at zero is not reconciling.

panels.title: Settlement ledger
panels.description: The settlement ledger (settle.redb) is what `decdn node earnings` reads. Write failures are rows decoded from a landed redeemMany that could not be written (disk full, store locked). Skipped rows are landed redemptions that produced no row for a reason other than paying nothing: a Settled log that does not decode or names no log index, a backfill whose block time or receipt the RPC could not supply, or a ledger read that failed; each is also a warn!. The redemption stands either way, but the earnings table silently trails the chain (`decdn node earnings --address` still reads the chain's record). DecdnSettlementLedgerWriteFailing alerts on write failures.

panels.title: Pools awaiting re-anchor
panels.description: Pools the settlement watcher seeded from one admission-time getPool (a pool whose PoolOpened lies below its scan start), or marked stale, and has not yet re-read at a pinned block. Set at the end of every watcher tick, after that tick's reads. It is an aggregate with no per-pool label: a value that never falls is a backlog that does not drain, either a pool that keeps failing to anchor (an open a reorg dropped, a read always skipped as stale, a read that keeps faulting) or new seeds replacing anchored ones; a steady anchored rate beside it is churn. Each pending pool costs one getPool per rotation. DecdnSettlementReanchorBacklog fires after 30m above 0.

panels.title: Re-anchor ticks that read no pool
panels.description: Re-anchor ticks that read no pool, so every pending pool waits for the next tick. Block read failed: the block-number read failed. Backend behind the watcher: the block number was below the highest log block the settlement watcher applied. Either one sustained points at the RPC provider.

panels.title: Re-anchor read outcomes
panels.description: Per-pool getPool reads at the pinned block. Anchored is the denominator for the rest. Pool read failed: the rest of the tick's batch waits; a steady rate with no RPC outage points at ABI drift on getPool. Absent: no pool at the pinned block (a backend behind the admit read, or an open a reorg dropped); the pool stays served from its seed. The skips are reads older than state the node holds: below a folded event; a lower totalRedeemed (a reorg lowered it, and the node refuses the pool early); a lower deposit (a reorg lowered it, and the node serves past the pool's funds, which the on-chain redeem caps; DecdnSettlementReanchorLowerDeposit). Failed, absent and skipped pools stay pending.

panels.title: Top-ups
panels.description: Background low-water top-ups that landed or failed. Nonce lost counts topUps whose nonce was spent with nothing escrowed: this node's seller redeemer signs redeemMany with the same key, so a redemption sent at the same moment took the nonce, and the node retries with a fresh topUp. A funding call that runs out of retries also counts as failed. A sustained nonce-lost rate means the redeemer and the buyer contend for the key's nonces.

panels.title: Pool-open failures by cause
panels.description: Sibling counters for the openPool tx. The aggregate decdn_node_pull_pool_open_failures_total on the delivery dashboard is larger: it also counts store, open-task, capability-signing and lane-seed causes that never reach a transaction. Buyer ledger integrity's lane seed failures are the lane-seed share.

panels.title: Buyer ledger integrity
panels.description: A skipped undecodable record is a buyer-pool row silently omitted from an otherwise successful store hydration, counted once per row per load. A lane seed failure is a pull refused because the lane's already-paid watermark could not be established: getWatermark failed or timed out, the buyer store faulted on a read under the seed lock, the buyer row vanished before or during the seed, or the store could not persist the seed. Each also counts as a pool open failure. A sustained rate means this node buys nothing from the affected providers. A pool adoption failure means bootstrap could not tell whether this node already owns a pool, so the first miss may escrow a second deposit; it runs once per process, so read it as a value since start.

panels.title: Unresolved on-chain holds
panels.description: 1 while this node holds its slot for an openPool or a topUp whose outcome the chain has not shown (the topUp hold is decdn v0.2): the submit got no tx hash or the receipt could not be read, and the transaction may still mine. A submit gets no tx hash when the transport fails and, from decdn v0.3.0, also when the RPC node already holds the transaction (`already known`), counts its nonce as spent (`nonce too low`) or holds another transaction of this key at that nonce (`replacement transaction underpriced`). Each of those can come back when a gateway retries a send that another backend already accepted, or when this node's own seller redemption took that nonce; the node then settles the nonce against the chain, and the hold ends once the redemption mines. Meanwhile the node sends no other transaction of that kind until a receipt arrives, the account's nonce passes it, or a re-send shows the pool closed. A hold that stays means the RPC cannot answer, a pending transaction holds the nonce or an earlier one, or every re-send at that nonce fails (the wallet cannot fund the amount or the gas); the daemon's repeating warning names the last failure in its `last` field. Do not restart a node holding a topUp slot: the restart forgets the hold, and the node may escrow a second topUp into its own pool. DecdnBuyerTopupUnresolved fires after 15m.

panels.title: Settlement and chain-RPC log lines
panels.description: The redeemMany revert / send-failed / receipt-failed / receipt-timeout cluster, plus the admit-path getPool and getAuthorization failures that make the node refuse revenue.

targets.expr: {unit="decdn-node.service", instance=~"$instance"} | json lvl="level", tgt="target", msg="fields.message" |~ "(?i)redeemmany|redeem|topup|top-up|getpool|getauthorization|slash" | lvl=~"WARN|ERROR" | line_format "{{.instance}} {{.lvl}} {{.tgt}} :: {{.msg}}"

panels.title: RPC requests by method
panels.description: JSON-RPC requests the node sent to blockchain.rpc_url, per method, from decdn_rpc_requests_total. Every provider the node builds counts here: watcher reads, filler lookups and transaction sends. Methods outside the fixed set count as other. The startup reachability probe and its watchdog are not provider requests; decdn_rpc_healthy reports them.

panels.title: RPC error ratio by method
panels.description: Share of JSON-RPC requests that failed, per method: every outcome other than ok and reverted, over all requests. A revert is the provider answering correctly that the call failed, so it is excluded. The all methods series is the ratio the DecdnRpcErrorRatioHigh alert reads. RPC failures by outcome breaks a spike down by cause.

panels.title: RPC failures by outcome
panels.description: Failed JSON-RPC requests per second, by outcome. rate_limited: the provider throttled the node (HTTP 429, Retry-After, or a rate-limit error code); raise the plan or lower the poll cadence. transport_error: no usable reply (refused or reset connection, HTTP 5xx, unreadable body). timeout: the request did not resolve before its deadline. rpc_error: any other JSON-RPC error response. On eth_getLogs that is a provider's transient error (such as "temporary internal error"), which the poller retries in place and defers to the next tick after the last retry, or a range cap, which shrinks the window; the eth_getLogs window span panel's retries/s and rejections/s tell them apart. While the watchers keep ticking, a steady rpc_error rate is an unreliable provider the node is absorbing. reverted: the call reverted; this is not a provider fault and is shown for context only.

panels.title: RPC latency p95 by method
panels.description: 95th-percentile round trip of a JSON-RPC request, per method, from decdn_rpc_request_duration_seconds. A request the caller dropped at its deadline records no sample and counts as a timeout in RPC failures by outcome, so read the two together: a flat p95 beside a rising timeout rate means a provider that answers some requests fast and never answers others.

title: deCDN — chain, payments and slash safety
